newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH shares fall after sales.
newsitem.headline: LVMH shares fall after sales.

text.p: Shares in French luxury goods group LVMH fell on Friday on disappointment with its 1996 sales and its profit warning for 1997 resulting from LVMH's acquisition of DFS, brokers said.
The stock was down 3.38 percent at 1,401 francs at 1520 GMT.

LVMH reported a 4.6 percent rise in sales for 1996 -- in line with market expectations -- but analysts said some of the details were disturbing, as was LVMH's warning of earnings per share dilution in 1997 from the acquisition of DFS.
It has acquired 61.25 percent of DFS for around $2.6 billion.

The company also held a conference call with analysts on Thursday evening after issuing the sales report which showed a drop of 3.3 percent in the perfumes and beauty products branch and a 7.4 percent drop in cognac and spirits sales due to weakness in Asian markets, notably Japan.
Sales rose 9.8 percent in the champagne and wines division and 21.6 percent in the luggage division -- the rise in the latter coming as a pleasant surprise to many analysts.
Analysts who participated in the conference call said LVMH sounded more cautious about the acquisition of DFS than it had previously.
"They seem to think that the financing conditions will be more expensive than they had calculated and that goodwill won't be at all what was anticipated," one analyst said.
In its sales statement on Thursday, the company said, "The acquisition should lead to growth on the order of 50 percent for sales and close to 30 percent for LVMH's operating profit."

The acquisition will have "a positive impact on net income from operations after income taxes but before amortization of goodwill, but a negative effect on reported net income after goodwill amortisation," it said.
It reiterated, however, that the acquisition was expected to boost consolidated sales by around 50 percent and income from operations by nearly 30 percent.
These forecasts, previously made, had fuelled rallies in LVMH shares when the deal was first announced in December and then again this month when it closed.
